[new component]{.chip .built} [measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 79 · milestone M4
:::

We tried a tighter bound calculation for the transport surrogates. The first
[output-bound run](78-output-bounds-and-unresolved-transport-limits.qmd) enclosed the
network outputs in their signed-log training units, but converting those intervals
back to flux overflowed. A [guard](../primer.qmd) needs finite physical
limits before it can use these certificates.

The follow-up uses alpha-CROWN, which optimizes the linear relaxations used to bound
the network. On each input box, we intersect its interval with ordinary CROWN and
interval propagation. Each interval encloses the same network, so their intersection
retains that enclosure while taking the tightest available endpoint. Interval
propagation also preserves the nonnegative range of the heat-flux heads.

The saved runs kept the original weights and complete input boxes. Their budgets
were [three optimizer iterations, a five-second soft budget per bound side and one leaf per member; both twenty-member runs finished within the nine-minute hard process limit]{.claim}[C-267](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-267){.cid .st-measured}. We did not narrow the domain or change the physical
acceptance contract.

| ensemble | training-space interval width relative to the first run |
|---|---|
| ITER | [median width 0.164 of the earlier bound, range 0.082–0.605 across member outputs; all twenty physical member results remain unknown]{.claim}[C-265](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-265){.cid .st-measured} |
| MAST-U | [median width 0.114 of the earlier bound, range 0.060–0.220 across member outputs; all twenty physical member results remain unknown]{.claim}[C-266](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-266){.cid .st-measured} |

These are comparisons of two budgeted runs: the optimized calculation used one leaf,
whereas the original CROWN calculation used four. The reductions therefore describe
the retained calculations, rather than isolating the effect of optimization.

Every member still has an upper or lower bound too large for the inverse signed-log
transform. The reports preserve the finite training-space bounds and explicitly mark
the physical result unknown. The larger numerical values are bounds produced by
relaxation; we have no counterexample showing that the network actually reaches them.

Before bounding, each member export is compared with JAX on random-box and held-out
inputs. The evidence audit checks the saved hashes, complete boxes, member outcomes
and overflow reasons. These checks share the toolkit's export and audit machinery;
they are not an independent implementation of the proof. The calculation concerns
real-valued networks represented by saved parameters, with float64 arithmetic and no
directed-rounding guarantee.

## What's next

V5 remains incomplete. Tighter physical transport bounds are still required for
certificate-bound guards. EC and pedestal keep their earlier finite enclosures, and
MAST-U's accepted certification limitation remains in force. Local robustness, the
EC coupled comparison and the owner's certification review remain ahead.
